title: [Prime] UGREEN 65W Nexode 3-Port GaN Charger $28.21 Delivered @ UGREEN via Amazon AU App
body:
Deal: [Prime] UGREEN 65W Nexode 3-Port GaN Charger $28.21 Delivered @ UGREEN via Amazon AU App

[ericshurn] Why would you get this over the Novoo? Just more reliable brand?
[beOson] I would think Anker > UGreen > the rest. I have both Anker and Ugreen, they are really good.
[Skele-Cr] I've tried Novoo and it seems also well built which is different to the Heymix ones that used to be on here a few years ago. That one just stopped working on me randomly after like 2 months, Novoo doesn't seem to do that so far.
[Shon] Extra port as well. But I really like my Novoo, seems well built.
[MediumRareChicken] I’d get the 67W Novoo for $19.99. Has the same amount of ports as this Ugreen
[Blitzfx] I got the Novoo because it's also thinner when plugging multiple plugs on a power board
[joe-john] I've got two of these for a few years, highly recommend. Build quality is pretty good, the sockets are very smooth to plug in, feels premium. I've used them as my main charger for my phone and NS switch, never missed a beat and charges pretty quick.
[ShinyDiamond] Motorola 68w charger at $32 is also a good option if you don't need type A. Comes with 1m cable as well. Listed at $37 but price beat brings down to $32.
https://www.thegoodguys.com.au/motorola-68w-adapter-with-usb…
[HaydosK] That's good but it doesn't clearly list specs. It's definitely GaN but idk how well it will work with other brands.
[heef] this one came with a Legion Tab i had. It is identical and worked fine with all my usbc devices, it js PD.
[HaydosK] Does it charge at the full rate of those devices though? For example Samsung and iPhone
[HaydosK] @heef: Ok that's good. It doesn't say that clearly on the site.
[heef] @HaydosK: Yeah true. This is the same one, just not an AU wall plug: https://support.lenovo.com/au/en/accessories/acc500325-overv…
independently tested: https://www.chargerlab.com/teardown-of-lenovo-68w-original-u…
[HaydosK] @heef: Wouldn't this be better? https://www.chargerlab.com/teardown-of-ugreen-65w-3-in-1-nex…
It seems to support more protocols
[Clear] @HaydosK: Is that one sold in Australia? I don't think so.
[HaydosK] @Clear: https://www.thegoodguys.com.au/ugreen-65w-3-port-robot-gan-f…
Clearly the price is for the smaller size and screen.
[Clear] @HaydosK: I stand corrected. My mistake was Googling the model number that TGG clearly don't use. Also a single USB-C charger vs a multiport isn't really comparable. If we were to compare based purely on a single USB-C port, then Motorola lands on top.
[HaydosK] @Clear: It's only a 3w difference. It can still do 65w on one port. Also it's good to have the option for USB A and USB C
[Clear] @HaydosK: It's also $54 vs $32. You should be comparing it to the charger in this deal where it's the same number/type of ports and cheaper at $28.21
[HaydosK] @Clear: Def the one in the post is a better deal but I think it uses older tech based on the size.
[Clear] @HaydosK: The only difference is that the CD361 for $52 has PPS output up to 11V/5A, while the CD244 for $28.21 has PPS output up to 11V/4.5A. Very minimal difference in the real world and certainly not worth the extra.
[michaelTito] Image says 89w but description says 68w.
Ummm?
[ce5himm] if you only clicked "redeem", it will be fine.
if you need to manually type "UGREEN10", normally no cashback.
[odb] I'm not sure about that. Can you clarify this? @tightarse
[MetalPhreak] I use these with the USB-C to barrel plug PD cables to replace all the crappy 12V plug packs. Then still have a bonus few USB 5V ports for stuff.
[Hiphopopotamus] That's kind of genius, never considered this before.
[reloxation] Out of interest, do those cables negotiate the volts/amps to deliver?
[trevor99] I got one of these for 31 last week now bought another with the code.
It's nice and heavy which is a good sign and works very well. 65w is a good size for many things. I rather have several of these on a power board for multiple devices rather than one with 8 ports or whatever.
[R4] Don't overthink it - it's a Chinese made phone charger, in a sea of many other Chinese made phone chargers. They all do the same thing for not much money. Just buy it.
[ozvictor] Was going to buy it to charge my S25 Ultra at 45W, but an Amazon review mentioned that it doesn't actually support Samsung's Super Fast Charging 2.0, not sure if this is correct as it would be a deal breaker to me.
"Be warned - the technical specs included in Amazon's product listing are for an updated version of this charger. I bought it so that I could have Super Fast Charging for my new Samsung Galaxy S24+ at 45W. For a charger to support Samsung's Super Fast Charging protocol for 45W, it must have an output of at least 4.05A. The tech specs in Amazon's product listing states that it satisfies Samsung's SFC protocol and has a 4.5A output. However, when the product arrived, the specs on the box state that the max output is 3.25A - so it doesn't meet Samsung's SFC protocol requirements"
